newsitem.title: DUBAI: OPEC's Lukman expects strong oil demand to continuE.
newsitem.headline: OPEC's Lukman expects strong oil demand to continuE.

text.p: OPEC Secretary General Rilwanu Lukman was on Tuesday quoted as saying strong demand for oil will continue this year and that OPEC felt comfortable with the current oil prices.
Lukman made his comments in an interview published by the London-based Arabic-language al-Hayat newspaper.

"We believe the strong demand on oil that we saw at the start of the current year will continue for a while and until demand from North America increases in the middle of the summer, prices will remain stable without declining a lot," Lukman said.

"From the strong indications we have on market demand we hope prices will continue at an acceptable level," he said. "We don't expect a sharp rise in prices...We don't believe prices will deteriorate and if they don't rise then for sure they will stay at reasonable levels which is what we hope."
He said OPEC members "always hope for better and more stable prices and if prices range between $22 and $25 a barrel then this is a good level."
"We don't feel uncomfortable with the current level of prices but we hope (prices) remain high in a reasonable and stable way," he said.

Asked if increasing production capacity of OPEC as well as non-OPEC members would lead to a supply surplus, Lukman said: "There is no problem, on the contrary there is need to increase the capacity of OPEC and non-OPEC members in the coming years.
"If OPEC does not raise its production capacity, there will be a shortage in surplus capacity within two to three years and then the prices will start going up," Lukman added.
He said conservative estimates expect the increase in oil demand over the next few years to average 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) to 1.6 million bpd and in some cases to 1.8 million bpd.
"And there is surplus production capacity currently in OPEC reaching, along with the Iraqi production, three to five million bpd," he said.
